title: How Succession, Reform and Revolution Rework Existing Structures
summary: Civilizations do not reach a new version only through breakdown. Succession can inherit capacities from an older system, reform can modify interfaces while retaining continuity, and revolution can alter legitimacy, institutions and resource allocation at the same time.
shortAnswer: Civilizations do not reach a new version only through breakdown. Succession can inherit capacities from an older system, reform can modify interfaces while retaining continuity, and revolution can alter legitimacy, institutions and resource allocation at the same time.

blocks.text: Civilizations do not reach a new version only through breakdown. Succession can inherit capacities from an older system, reform can modify interfaces while retaining continuity, and revolution can alter legitimacy, institutions and resource allocation at the same time.

The purpose is not to rank the three paths, but to observe what each preserves, what it replaces, and where transition costs fall. Succession, reform and revolution can also overlap within the same historical period.

This article uses only definitions and structural relations in the completed Book VI manuscript. Conceptual boundaries are not presented as additional historical facts, and no new causal claims are added beyond the manuscript.
